finding: CPR annotations represent reduction of P450 heme states, whereas the FNS-II reaction represents reductase-bound flavin donor states. These participant identities are distinct and cannot be canceled as an exact stoichiometric join.
evidence_boundary: All three catalytic annotations are automated. Predicted membrane and flavin-binding features are retained with evidence codes; they do not prove compatibility with an FNS-II lead.
next_requirements: Recover characterized plant CPR reference sequences for an independent full-proteome comparison.
Reconcile explicit carrier states and electron/proton accounting before constructing a coupled net equation.
Measure paired P450/CPR turnover with NADPH and authentic products, retaining P450-only, CPR-only and no-NADPH controls.
claim_boundary: No native partnership or net conversion is established. Do not replace carrier identities with free flavin or heme, or infer missing reductase absence from a name-only inventory.
